source_text: From 110 F0 females collected from the field 7 were homozygous resistant (RR) (6.3%), 48 were heterozygous (RS) (43.2%) and 55 were homozygous susceptible (SS) (49.5%). Overall, the frequency of the 119F resistant allele was 28 and 72% for the L119 susceptible allele.

inconsistency_note: RR+RS+SS = 90 (3+12+75) but N = 92; printed percentage for SS (83.7%) corresponds to 77/92, suggesting SS = 75 is a typo for 77.
source_text: Out of the 92 samples genotyped, 3 were RR (3.2%), 12 were RS (13.1%) and 75 were SS (83.7%) with frequency of resistant allele of only 9.7% and susceptible allele of 90.3%.
Out of 72 samples genotyped, 22 were RR (30.5%) 48 were RS (66.6%) and 2 were SS (2.7%) with frequency of the resistant allele 1014F of 63.9% and the susceptible L1014 allele of 36.1%.
Out of the 76 samples genotyped for the L1014S marker, 3 were RS (3.9%) and 73 were SS (96.1%), thus a very low frequency of 1.97% was recorded for the resistance allele.
Out of 50 samples genotyped, neither RR nor RS were detected as all the samples were found to be SS.
